title: God doesn’t respond to noise.
paragraphs:
God doesn’t respond to noise.
He responds to hearts.

Not louder prayers.
Not longer speeches.
Not perfect words.
He listens for something deeper.
Here are 5 types of hearts God responds to—and one of them might expose you.

1. The Broken Heart
Not polished. Not pretending.
Shattered.
“The Lord is close to the brokenhearted…” (Psalm 34:18)

This is the heart that finally stops performing.
The one that says, “God, I can’t fix this.”
And that’s where He steps in.

2. The Repentant Heart
Not defensive. Not justifying.
Turning.
“A broken and contrite heart… you will not despise.” (Psalm 51:17)

Repentance isn’t guilt—it’s surrender.
It’s saying, “I was wrong. Your way is better.”
And heaven moves when pride falls.

3. The Humble Heart
Not entitled. Not demanding.
Kneeling.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” (James 4:6)

You don’t impress God with status.
You meet Him at the ground.
Grace flows downhill.

4. The Faith-Filled Heart
Not seeing. Still believing.
Holding on.
“Without faith it is impossible to please God…” (Hebrews 11:6)

This is the heart that trusts
even when prayers feel unanswered.

Not blind hope—
but anchored confidence in who God is.

5. The Surrendered Heart
Not controlling. Not resisting.
Yielded.
“Not my will, but Yours be done.” (Luke 22:42)

This is where Jesus won the battle—
not on the cross first…
…but in surrender.
But here’s what we miss…

You can act broken.
You can sound humble.
You can talk faith.
But God sees the real condition.
And still—He invites you closer.

Because the Gospel isn’t about perfect hearts.
It’s about dead hearts made alive through Jesus.

Sin hardened us.
Grace breaks us open.
The cross restores us.

So come as you are—
but don’t stay as you are.
Let Him change your heart.
